message.content:
A CPU (Central Processing Unit) and a GPU (Graphics Processing Unit) are both processors, but they’re designed for different kinds of workloads:

| Feature | CPU | GPU |
|---------|-----|-----|
| **Primary purpose** | General‑purpose computing – handles everything from OS tasks to application logic. | Parallel graphics rendering – originally for rasterizing images, now also used for massively parallel compute tasks. |
| **Architecture** | Few cores (typically 2–32) optimized for low latency, complex control flow, and large caches. | Hundreds to thousands of simpler cores optimized for throughput and SIMD (single instruction, multiple data). |
| **Instruction set** | Complex, rich instruction set with branch prediction, out‑of‑order execution, large L1/L2/L3 caches. | Simpler, often fixed‑function pipelines; many cores share small caches or rely on fast shared memory. |
| **Memory hierarchy** | Large private caches per core, sophisticated memory controllers, high cache hit rates. | Smaller per‑core caches, but very fast shared memory (e.g., CUDA shared memory) and high bandwidth global memory. |
| **Typical workloads** | Sequential tasks, branching logic, I/O, OS services, single‑threaded performance. | Data‑parallel tasks: matrix multiplications, image/video processing, machine‑learning inference/training, scientific simulations. |
| **Performance characteristics** | High single‑thread performance, low latency. | High throughput for many identical operations, high memory bandwidth. |
| **Programming model** | Traditional CPU programming (C/C++, Java, etc.) with threads, processes, and OS scheduling. | Parallel programming models (CUDA, OpenCL, DirectX, Vulkan, Metal) that expose many lightweight threads. |

In short, a CPU excels at tasks that require complex decision making and low latency, while a GPU shines when you can break a problem into many identical, independent operations that can run in parallel. That’s why GPUs are now common in AI training, scientific computing, and even general‑purpose GPU (GPGPU) applications.
